comparisons.peer_summary: AMD develops world-class software stacks, including tools, compilers, and drivers, and works with customers to define customized solutions using its IP and design leadership.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and NVIDIA identify software stacks and development tools as critical components enabling their hardware platforms, though NVIDIA specifically links its strategy to computer graphics infused with AI, while AMD emphasizes a broad high-performance stack and custom solutions. NVIDIA states, 'Our technologies are instrumental in driving the gaming, design, and creative industries forward... on our GeForce and NVIDIA RTX platforms,' highlighting graphics and AI integration. Similarly, AMD declares, 'We develop world-class software stacks that are used to enable our high-performance products,' noting that these stacks include tools and drivers for its various processors.

sentences.text: Our technologies are instrumental in driving the gaming, design, and creative industries forward, as developers leverage our libraries and algorithms to deliver an optimized experience on our GeForce and NVIDIA RTX platforms.
We develop world-class software stacks that are used to enable our high-performance products.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company provides advanced technology and IP platforms for customers to design ASICs targeting AI, high-performance computing, and networking applications.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and Broadcom (Avago) highlight their capability to provide customized silicon solutions for advanced workloads like AI, though NVIDIA frames this within its broader graphics and AI ecosystem strategy while Broadcom focuses on custom ASICs. NVIDIA describes its RTX platforms and Tensor Cores as central to its graphics and AI business. Broadcom states, 'Custom Silicon Solutions: We provide advanced technology and intellectual property ("IP") platforms for customers to design and develop application specific integrated circuits ("ASICs") targeting AI and high-performance computing,' showing a shared focus on specialized hardware for AI but through different architectural approaches (RTX GPUs vs. Custom ASICs).

sentences.text: Our computer graphics platforms leverage AI end-to-end, from the developer tools and cloud services to the Tensor Cores included in all RTX-class GPUs.

• Custom Silicon Solutions: We provide advanced technology and intellectual property ("IP") platforms for customers to design and develop application specific integrated circuits ("ASICs") targeting AI and high-performance computing, networking and storage applications. Our custom silicon provides the platform to integrate embedded logic, memory, serializer/deserializer ("SerDes") technology, IP cores and processor cores. ASICs are custom products built to individual customers specifications.

comparisons.peer_topic: Software strategy and open source contributions
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel aims to optimize AI frameworks and maintains the OpenVINO toolkit for deep learning inference. In 2024, Intel launched the Open Platform for Enterprise AI under the Linux Foundation and contributed oneAPI specifications to the UXL Foundation to enable open, multi-vendor programming across accelerators.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and Intel emphasize that software is essential to unlock the potential of their hardware, with both companies developing specific software frameworks to support AI and general workloads. NVIDIA asserts, 'We believe that computer graphics infused with AI is fundamental to the continued expansion and evolution of computing,' linking software/AI directly to its graphics strategy. Intel complements this with, 'Software unleashes the potential of our hardware platforms across all workloads, domains, and architectures,' and details its OpenVINO toolkit for deep learning inference, mirroring NVIDIA's focus on software-algorithm integration for performance.

sentences.text: We believe that computer graphics infused with AI is fundamental to the continued expansion and evolution of computing.
Software unleashes the potential of our hardware platforms across all workloads, domains, and architectures.

Our OpenVINO™ toolkit is an open source toolkit that accelerates deep learning inference on our processors across various use cases, such as generative AI, computer vision, audio, and language with industry standard models.

comparisons.peer_summary: The graphics market is driven by AI, VR/AR, and high-resolution gaming needs; the company announced GDDR7 in 2024, completing its industry-leading portfolio for AI inference on CPUs, NPUs, and GPUs.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and Micron (MU) explicitly address the graphics market and its drivers, specifically identifying AI and gaming as key forces. NVIDIA describes its strategy around 'computer graphics infused with AI' and platforms for 'gaming, design, and creative industries.' Micron supports this by stating, 'Graphics: The graphics market is driven by the need for high-performance and HBM solutions,' and notes that its graphics products are 'the driving force behind applications such as AI... gaming.' This shows a shared recognition of the graphics sector's composition and its convergence with AI needs.

Our GDDR6 and GDDR6X DRAM graphics products are incorporated into gaming consoles, PC graphics cards, and graphics processing unit-based data center solutions, which are the driving force behind applications such as AI, virtual and augmented reality, 4K and 8K gaming, and professional design.

comparisons.peer_topic: Processor architecture and AI Engine capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm utilizes System-on-Chip architecture with heterogeneous computing, including Oryon and Kryo CPUs and Adreno GPUs, to enable high-performance, low-power computing. The Qualcomm AI Engine features dedicated hardware and the Hexagon NPU for high-performance on-device AI inference, supported by the AI Stack and AI Hub to simplify developer integration.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and Qualcomm discuss the role of Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) and specialized AI hardware in delivering high-performance computing, though NVIDIA focuses on data center/PC graphics (RTX) while Qualcomm focuses on mobile SoC graphics and NPUs. NVIDIA highlights 'Tensor Cores included in all RTX-class GPUs' for AI. Qualcomm states, 'Our Qualcomm® Adreno™ GPUs are designed to deliver high quality graphics performance... The Qualcomm® AI Engine... includes dedicated hardware capable of running complex AI use cases,' reflecting a shared industry trend of integrating dedicated AI hardware alongside graphics capabilities across different form factors.

sentences.text: Our computer graphics platforms leverage AI end-to-end, from the developer tools and cloud services to the Tensor Cores included in all RTX-class GPUs.
Our Qualcomm® Adreno™ GPUs are designed to deliver high quality graphics performance for visually rich 3D gaming and user interfaces.

The Qualcomm® AI Engine, featured in our Snapdragon platforms and many of our other products, includes dedicated hardware capable of running complex AI use cases at high-performance and low-power on device, while also enhancing privacy and security.
